solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Crazed gang’s boss made good, finally (9)

indicatorNotes.finally: takes the final letter of each of the words before it

blocks.note: a posse is a gang; with the 's it reads POSSE'S
last letters of boss, made, good

annotation.surface: A gang leader went straight at last.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'good' makes 'made good' look like a phrase about reform; really 'finally' strips the last letter from three separate words.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone possessed is acting as if taken over, wild or crazed.

entries.clue: Stand firm with co-director? (11)

blocks.note: the reading the surface pushes: hold your ground, refuse to budge
the reading the setter means: 'firm' is a business, and one where each boss stands alongside another as an equal owner

annotation.surface: Advice to hold your ground alongside a fellow boss.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stand firm' reads as one phrase meaning hold out; split it and 'firm' is a business, one owned jointly by co-directors.
annotation.definitionFit: A partnership is a firm owned and run by two or more partners.

entries.clue: Cunning, extremely spiritual cardinal (7)

indicatorNotes.extremely: takes the extremes, the first and last letters, of the next word

blocks.note: first and last letters of spiritual
a cardinal number

annotation.surface: A wily prince of the church who is very pious.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' paints a churchman beside 'spiritual', but here it is a cardinal number, as opposed to an ordinal like eighth.
annotation.definitionFit: Sleight is skill in deception, as in sleight of hand, so cunning.

entries.clue: Consistent time for the 100m, perhaps (5)

blocks.note: even = steady, consistent
t = time

annotation.surface: A sprinter posting the same time in every 100m race.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is by example, flagged by 'perhaps': the 100m is one event at an athletics meeting.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an athletics meeting is made up of events, and the 100m sprint is one of them.

entries.clue: Taint of guilt besetting each top naval bigwig (3,7)

indicatorNotes.besetting: to beset is to surround, so STAIN goes round the next letters

blocks.note: a stain on one's character
ea. = each
a cap is a top, as on a bottle

annotation.surface: A disgraced admiral whose guilt clings to every senior officer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taint of guilt' reads as a moral judgement on the officers; it is simply STAIN, and 'top' is a lid rather than rank.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: the master of a ship is the big man aboard, and 'naval' stretches to cover any seagoing command.

entries.clue: Brush aside senior cop’s bad shot (7)

blocks.note: DI = Detective Inspector, plus the 's
a shot that misses

annotation.surface: A top detective shrugging off a poor bit of shooting.
annotation.walkthrough: A DI (Detective Inspector) is a senior British police rank.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: waving away an objection without considering it is both brushing it aside and dismissing it.

entries.clue: A locum tenens principally reads out systems of names (13)

indicatorNotes.principally: takes the principal, first, letter of reads
indicatorNotes.out: out = wrong, broken, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters
first letter of reads

annotation.surface: A stand-in doctor reading out the list of names.
annotation.walkthrough: A locum tenens is a stand-in, usually a doctor; the Latin makes the phrase feel like a technical term, which hides that it is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A nomenclature is a system of naming, as in botany.

entries.clue: Charlotte’s place adjacent to Virginia? (5,8)

blocks.note: the reading the surface pushes: the home of a woman called Charlotte; the setter means the US city of that name
the reading the setter means: not a neighbour of a woman called Virginia but a territory sharing a border with the US state

annotation.surface: Two women, Charlotte and Virginia, sitting side by side.
annotation.walkthrough: Charlotte and Virginia look like two women's names; they are a US city and the state along North Carolina's northern border.
annotation.definitionFit: Charlotte is in North Carolina, which lies just south of Virginia.

entries.clue: Spy caper almost broken by copper focusing on the tiniest details (9)

indicatorNotes.almost: drops the last letter of LARK
indicatorNotes.broken by: the string MOLE LAR is split open to let CU in

blocks.note: a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
LARK = caper, less its last letter

annotation.surface: A spy's scheme nearly wrecked by a policeman with an eye for detail.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman beside 'spy caper', but it is the element. The break falls exactly at the join between the spy and the shortened caper.
annotation.definitionFit: Molecular means at the level of molecules, so concerned with the tiniest parts.

entries.clue: Close relatives live in comfortable home (7)

annotation.definitionNote: as in 'nearest and dearest', one's nearest being one's close family

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' as a preposition of place: one thing is in another when it sits inside it, so ARE goes inside NEST

blocks.note: a cosy home
to be, to exist: they are

annotation.surface: Family members living together in a snug house.
annotation.walkthrough: NE(ARE)ST. 'Live' has to be read as 'exist', which gives ARE.
annotation.definitionFit: Your nearest are your closest family, as in the phrase 'nearest and dearest'.

entries.clue: Influential figure in heavy metal initially is noticeably gentle, not heavy (7,5)

indicatorNotes.initially: takes the first letters of the next three words

blocks.note: lead is a heavy metal
first letters of is, noticeably, gentle
light = not heavy

annotation.surface: A heavy metal star who is surprisingly soft-spoken.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' reads as the music genre; here it is the chemical element lead.
annotation.definitionFit: A leading light is a prominent, influential person in a field.

entries.clue: Human being’s terrible ill nature (9)

indicatorNotes.terrible: the letters are in a terrible state, so they get rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

annotation.surface: Mankind's terrible bad temper.
annotation.walkthrough: A rare word: a tellurian is an inhabitant of the Earth, from Latin tellus, earth.
annotation.definitionFit: A learned word for an earth-dweller, from Latin tellus, earth, used in science fiction for humans as opposed to aliens.

entries.clue: Inspired poet seen in Paris, historically (5)

indicatorNotes.seen in: the answer can be seen inside the next words

blocks.note: paRIS HIstorically

annotation.surface: A poet who found inspiration in old Paris.
annotation.walkthrough: A rishi is an inspired sage or poet of the Vedic hymns; 'historically' fits both the hidden word and the ancient role.
annotation.definitionFit: The rishis were the inspired poet-seers of the Hindu Vedas.

entries.clue: Irregularity of line taken out of choke point (11)

indicatorNotes.taken out of: the L is removed from the letters that follow

blocks.note: STRANGLE = choke, with L (line) taken out
a ness is a headland, a point of land
L = line, the letter removed

annotation.surface: A crooked line cut from a traffic bottleneck.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Choke point' reads as a single bottleneck; split it into STRANGLE and NESS. The L leaves only the first half.
annotation.definitionFit: Strangeness is oddity, a departure from the regular.

entries.clue: Former local representative concerned with one who raised Cain (5)

blocks.note: re = concerning
Eve was the mother of Cain in Genesis

annotation.surface: An old councillor linked to a troublemaker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised Cain' is an idiom for making trouble; read literally, Eve raised her son Cain. A reeve was a medieval local official.
annotation.definitionFit: A reeve was the chief officer of a town or district in medieval England.

entries.clue: Gold, extravagantly artisanal objects from down under (11)

indicatorNotes.extravagantly: the letters are treated extravagantly, thrown about

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
anagram of ARTISANAL

annotation.surface: Lavish gold handicrafts brought back from Australia.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Artisanal objects' reads as one phrase for handicrafts; only 'artisanal' is fodder, and 'objects from down under' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Australiana are things characteristic of Australia, down under being Australia.

entries.clue: Unsuccessful candidate somewhat irresolutely making a comeback (5)

indicatorNotes.somewhat: only some of the word is used

blocks.note: five letters from the middle of the word, starting after irr

annotation.surface: A hesitant politician trying to return after defeat.
annotation.walkthrough: The irresolute candidate attempting a comeback is exactly the kind of loser the answer names.
annotation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who failed to win, such as a beaten candidate.

entries.clue: I’m thrashing all over the place — very frightening (11)

indicatorNotes.all over the place: the letters are scattered all over the place

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 11 letters

annotation.surface: Someone flailing wildly in a terrifying scene.
annotation.walkthrough: Thrashing about all over the place is what you do in a nightmare, so the surface acts out the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Nightmarish means like a bad dream: very frightening.

entries.clue: Change of direction inspires a French non-profit organisation (6,5)

indicatorNotes.Change of: a change of the letters of direction
indicatorNotes.inspires: to inspire is to breathe in, so the rearranged letters take UN inside

blocks.note: anagram of DIRECTION, split to hold UN
un = a in French

annotation.surface: A French charity taking a new course.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Change of direction' reads as a single phrase for a U-turn; really 'change of' works on the letters of DIRECTION, which become CREDIT(UN)ION.
annotation.definitionFit: A credit union is a co-operative savings and loans body run for its members, not for profit.

entries.clue: You shouldn’t have repeatedly run around knocking (3-1-3)

indicatorNotes.around: turns TATATA the other way round

blocks.note: r = run, as on a cricket scorecard
TA is British for thank you, the reply to 'you shouldn't have', said three times

annotation.surface: Someone thanking a host over and over while running about at the door.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have!' is what you say on receiving a present; TA is the British thanks it stands for.
annotation.definitionFit: Rat-a-tat is the sound of repeated knocking on a door.

entries.clue: Stylish person, gathering endless looks, became popular (4,3)

blocks.note: a toff is a smart upper-class person
LOOKS with first and last letters removed

annotation.surface: A fashionable figure drawing admiring glances becomes a hit.
annotation.walkthrough: T(OOK)OFF. 'Endless' here means without either end, not just the last letter. A toff is British slang for a posh, well-dressed person.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that took off suddenly became successful or popular.

entries.clue: Quietly set aside bulb (7)

blocks.note: sh! = be quiet
to allot is to assign or set aside

annotation.surface: Discreetly putting a bulb to one side.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a light bulb; it is the onion kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A shallot is a small onion-like bulb.

entries.clue: Spot politicians involved in grand act of perjury (7)

indicatorNotes.involved in: the MPs are placed inside LIE

blocks.note: G = grand, a thousand pounds
perjury is lying under oath
MPs = Members of Parliament

annotation.surface: Catching sight of MPs caught up in a big perjury scandal.
annotation.walkthrough: G + LI(MPS)E. 'Grand' is an adjective in the surface, but here it is slang for a thousand, giving G.
annotation.definitionFit: To spot something is to glimpse it, see it briefly.

entries.clue: Hot meats go with a so-so Mexican chilli in the end (9)

indicatorNotes.in the end: takes the end letter of each of the three words

blocks.note: go = energy, pep
a = per, as in 'once a day'
last letters of so-so, Mexican, chilli

annotation.surface: Spicy meats served alongside an ordinary Mexican chilli.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Go' has to be read as a noun meaning energy, and 'a' as per; the Mexican chilli is pure decoration beyond its last letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy sausage, cut into slices of hot meat.
annotation.definitionNote: pepperoni is a mass noun, so 'meats' stands for slices of it

entries.clue: That’s funny … promising crooners butchered series of numbers (8,11)

blocks.note: ha! is what you say at something funny
anagram of PROMISING CROONERS, 17 letters

annotation.surface: Laughing as talented singers murder a run of songs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Funny' looks like an anagram indicator, but 'That's funny' is the laugh HA; 'butchered' does the rearranging. 'Series of numbers' also teases songs.
annotation.definitionFit: A mathematical term: a sequence whose reciprocals rise evenly, like 1, 1/2, 1/3, so a series of numbers in the maths sense.

entries.clue: Underlying reason to be frugal with booze (9)

blocks.note: to ration something is to use it sparingly
ale is beer

annotation.surface: The real reason for going easy on the drink.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface asks why someone would cut down on drink; the answer is the word for any such reason, built from the cutting down itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A rationale is the reasoning that underlies a decision.

entries.clue: Painter about to fill in survey, certainly (7)

indicatorNotes.to fill in: to fill something in is to occupy its empty middle, so C takes the space inside OK

blocks.note: an opinion poll is a survey
OK = certainly, all right
c. = circa, about

annotation.surface: An artist about to complete a questionnaire.
annotation.walkthrough: POLL + O(C)K. 'About to' reads as 'on the point of', but 'about' is C and 'to fill in' is the instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: Jackson Pollock was the American drip painter.

entries.clue: Postpone financial outlay outside America (7)

indicatorNotes.outside: 'outside' as a preposition: one thing outside another encloses it, so SPEND wraps round US

blocks.note: spend = money paid out, as in 'government spend'
the US

annotation.surface: Delaying spending money abroad in America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outside America' reads as spending abroad; it is a container instruction, with the country tucked inside the outlay.
annotation.definitionFit: To suspend something is to put it off for a time.

entries.clue: Food prices periodically dropped (3)

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters, losing the second, fourth and sixth

annotation.surface: Food costs fell from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as news of falling food prices; 'periodically dropped' is the instruction to lose every second letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: pie, a filling baked in pastry, is one kind of food, so the general word stands for it.

entries.clue: Ways to embrace love and compassion (6)

indicatorNotes.to embrace: to embrace is to hug, arms wrapped round someone, so PATHS wrap round O

blocks.note: paths are ways
love = zero in tennis, so O

annotation.surface: Advice on how to accept love and kindness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Love and compassion' reads as a pair; 'love' belongs to the wordplay and 'and' is only the joint before the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality that stirs pity, and so compassion, in an audience.

entries.clue: Tree next to a lake in the mountains (6)

indicatorNotes.next to: PINE goes next to, after, A L

blocks.note: as written
L = lake on maps
a pine tree

annotation.surface: A pine standing by a lake high in the mountains.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue reads tree first, but 'next to' lets PINE follow A and L.
annotation.definitionFit: Alpine means of high mountains, as in the Alps.

entries.clue: Shot that can’t be taken in the dark? (8,5)

annotation.definition: Shot that can’t be taken in the dark?

blocks.note: the reading the surface pushes: a photograph; the setter means an attempt at an answer

blocks.clueFragment: that can’t be taken in the dark?
blocks.note: the reading the setter means: the idiom 'a shot in the dark', a blind attempt, turned on its head

annotation.surface: A photographer unable to shoot without light.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' and 'dark' paint photography; a shot is also an attempt, and a shot in the dark is a blind guess, so an informed one is not taken in the dark.
annotation.definitionFit: An educated guess is an attempt at an answer based on some knowledge, not a blind one.

entries.clue: Boats in which Sydneysiders can have beers? (9)

annotation.definition2: in which Sydneysiders can have beers

blocks.note: a schooner is a sailing ship

blocks.clueFragment: in which Sydneysiders can have beers
blocks.note: in Australia a schooner is a large beer glass

annotation.surface: Australians drinking beer on board sailing boats.
annotation.walkthrough: The beer sense is regional: in New South Wales a schooner is a standard glass of beer, in Britain a large sherry glass.
annotation.definitionFit: Schooners are two-masted sailing vessels, and also beer glasses in Sydney.

entries.clue: Wild animals working long periods around river (7)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' as in surrounding: AGES is placed round R, enclosing it

blocks.note: on = working, switched on
ages = long spells of time
r = river

annotation.surface: Wild beasts toiling for ages beside a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working long periods' reads as overtime; split it into two plain pieces. An onager is a wild ass of Asia.
annotation.definitionFit: Onagers are wild asses of central Asia.

entries.clue: Drinks in club consumed by prison officers (12)

indicatorNotes.consumed by: the club is swallowed by SCREWS

blocks.note: screw is British slang for a prison warder
a driver is a golf club

annotation.surface: Warders drinking in their social club.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a place to drink; it is a golf club. A screwdriver is vodka and orange juice.
annotation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a cocktail of vodka and orange juice.

entries.clue: How things may come through the post? (2,7)

annotation.definition: How things may come through the post?

blocks.note: the reading the surface pushes: the route by which letters and parcels arrive
the reading the setter means: 'post' is a job or office, and things such as a seat on a board can come with it, in Latin

annotation.surface: Wondering how letters arrive through the letterbox.
annotation.walkthrough: 'The post' suggests mail; here it is a job or office, and ex officio powers come with the post.
annotation.definitionFit: Ex officio is Latin for by virtue of one's position or office.

entries.clue: Secret coup arranged to entrap one Brexiteer? (11)

indicatorNotes.arranged: the letters of SECRET COUP are rearranged
indicatorNotes.to entrap: the rearranged letters take I inside

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
I = one, the Roman numeral

annotation.surface: A covert plot to snare a Leave campaigner.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a Brexiteer is one kind of Eurosceptic.
annotation.definitionFit: A Brexiteer, who backed Britain leaving the EU, is a Eurosceptic.

entries.clue: Commercial introducing Clio possibly provided some laughs (6)

indicatorNotes.introducing: to introduce is literally to lead inside, so AD brings MUSE inside itself

blocks.note: an ad is a commercial
Clio is the Muse of history, one of nine

annotation.surface: An advert for the Renault Clio that gave viewers a laugh.
annotation.walkthrough: Clio looks like the Renault car in an advert; it is the Greek Muse of history, and 'possibly' flags her as one example of a Muse.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb phrase for a verb: the past tense amused covers having entertained people, giving them a few laughs.

entries.clue: Bar before long is accommodating more or less everybody (6)

indicatorNotes.is accommodating: to accommodate guests is to give them room inside, so SOON houses AL
indicatorNotes.more or less: ALL is nearly complete, losing a letter

blocks.note: soon = before long
ALL = everybody, less its last letter

annotation.surface: A pub that will soon be serving almost everyone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bar' could be a verb, to exclude, which would clash with accommodating everybody; it is the noun, a place to drink.
annotation.definitionFit: A saloon is a bar, especially the smarter room of a British pub.

entries.clue: Flyer nearly beginning to tumble during strong wind (11)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: takes the first letter of tumble
indicatorNotes.during: during = IN, a word that becomes letters here

blocks.note: nigh = nearly, as in 'well nigh'
first letter of tumble
during = in
a gale is a strong wind

annotation.surface: A pilot almost starting to fall in a gale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flyer' suggests a pilot; it is a bird. 'During' supplies IN as a straight piece, not a container.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: any bird is a flyer, and the nightingale, famous for singing at night, is one.

entries.clue: Naked obedientiary in disarray, drunk (10)

indicatorNotes.Naked: stripped of its outer letters O and Y
indicatorNotes.in disarray: the remaining letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: OBEDIENTIARY without its first and last letters, then rearranged

annotation.surface: A monk with no clothes on, dishevelled and drunk.
annotation.walkthrough: An obedientiary is a monastery office-holder, so the surface is a scandal at the abbey.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in a formal register: inebriated, from Latin ebrius, drunk, is the polite word for being the worse for drink.

entries.clue: Light breeze over valley (3)

blocks.note: an air is a gentle breeze

annotation.surface: A gentle wind blowing across a valley.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as 'above the valley'; it is the reversal instruction. A ria is a river valley drowned by the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A ria is a long, narrow inlet formed by the flooding of a river valley.

entries.clue: Nefarious activity began in kindergarten, strangely (8,3,8)

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 19 letters

annotation.surface: A criminal career that started at nursery school.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a villain's backstory, which is why the crime fits so neatly.
annotation.definitionFit: Breaking and entering is the crime of forcing entry to a building.

entries.clue: Part of the head requiring type of strapped support as a precaution (9)

blocks.note: a bra is supported by straps
in case = as a precaution

annotation.surface: A head injury that calls for a strapped brace just to be safe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Strapped support' suggests a medical brace; it is underwear.
annotation.definitionFit: The braincase is the part of the skull enclosing the brain.

entries.clue: Deputy — increasingly insensitive — also yelled out (6,3)

indicatorNotes.yelled out: said out loud, so what counts is the sound

blocks.note: more numb
too = also, spoken

annotation.surface: A deputy growing harder by the day and shouting as well.
annotation.walkthrough: NUMBER here is NUMB-ER, the comparative of numb, not the word for a figure.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal idiom: the person ranked second in an organisation, who stands in for the boss, is its number two.

entries.clue: Official charge follows this significant fine ultimately (7)

indicatorNotes.follows: WARD comes after the other letters
indicatorNotes.ultimately: takes the last letter of each of the three words

blocks.note: last letters of this, significant, fine
a ward is someone in your charge

annotation.surface: An official penalty following a hefty fine.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as fines and charges; 'charge' is a person in someone's care, and 'ultimately' picks up just S, T, E.
annotation.definitionFit: A steward is an official, such as one who runs a race meeting or an estate.

entries.clue: Very big and small parts of a pinball table (7)

blocks.note: bumper = unusually large, as in a bumper crop
s = small, as on clothes labels

annotation.surface: Big and little components of a pinball machine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very big and small' reads as a size range; it is BUMPER plus the S for small.
annotation.definitionFit: Bumpers are the sprung posts on a pinball table that bounce the ball away.

entries.clue: One tweeting obscene tirades is tactless, first and foremost (4,3)

indicatorNotes.first and foremost: takes the first letters of the three words before it

blocks.note: blue = smutty, as in a blue joke
first letters of tirades, is, tactless

annotation.surface: A social-media user posting crude rants without any tact.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tweeting' paints a person on social media; the answer is a bird that really tweets.
annotation.definitionFit: A blue tit is a small songbird, one that tweets.

entries.clue: Southern artist upset fellow artist (7)

indicatorNotes.upset: turned upside down, which in a down clue reverses RA

blocks.note: s = south
RA = Royal Academician, an artist, turned over
a gent is a man, a fellow

annotation.surface: A painter from the South offended a fellow painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Artist' appears twice: the first is RA, the second the definition. 'Fellow' looks like it qualifies the artist but is GENT.
annotation.definitionFit: John Singer Sargent was an American portrait painter.

entries.clue: Vehicle that is on left of street with the most traffic? (7)

indicatorNotes.on left of: in an across answer, to the left means earlier, so BUS IE come before ST

blocks.note: a bus is a vehicle
i.e. = id est, that is
St = street

annotation.surface: A bus parked on the left of the most congested road.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is road traffic, and the answer describes that road, hence the question mark.
annotation.definitionFit: The superlative of busy, used of roads carrying a lot of vehicles, so the one with the most traffic.

entries.clue: Country’s victories regularly overlooked in time (7)

indicatorNotes.regularly overlooked: every other letter is passed over
indicatorNotes.in: the kept letters go inside ERA

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
vIcToRiEs: skip v, c, o, i, s

annotation.surface: A nation whose wins are routinely forgotten over time.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's reads as 'has', linking definition and wordplay. 'Regularly' here keeps the even letters, not the odd ones.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: Eritrea, on the Red Sea in the Horn of Africa, is one of the world's countries.

entries.clue: Former writer desperate to claim trade union disbursement (11)

indicatorNotes.to claim: to claim something is to take hold of it, so DIRE takes TU into its grasp

blocks.note: ex = former
a pen writes
dire = desperate
TU = trade union

annotation.surface: An ex-author desperate to get money from the union.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Former writer' looks like one retired author; it splits into two pieces, and the writer is an object, not a person.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a disbursement is a paying out of money, which is what expenditure means in accounts.

entries.clue: Attach grips to mountaineering kit (5)

indicatorNotes.grips: PIN grips TO between its letters

blocks.note: to pin is to attach
as written

annotation.surface: Clipping holds on to climbing gear.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'to' that looks like a link word is the letters TO.
annotation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike driven into rock by climbers.

entries.clue: Early development of bug originally impacting people (11)

indicatorNotes.originally: takes the original, first, letter of impacting

blocks.note: a bug is an illness or a germ
first letter of impacting
a people is a nation

annotation.surface: The early spread of a virus that first hit the population.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is an epidemic; the answer is about seeds sprouting.
annotation.definitionFit: Germination is the first stage of a seed's growth, early development.

entries.clue: Support raised to bolster an investor (5)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raised means written upwards, so reversed
indicatorNotes.to bolster: GEL props up AN from below, so comes after it

blocks.note: as written
a leg supports a table

annotation.surface: Raising funds to back a backer.
annotation.walkthrough: An angel is someone who invests in a theatre production or start-up.
annotation.definitionFit: An angel is a private backer, especially of a show or a new business.

entries.clue: Plate traditionally including fish (5)

blocks.note: plaTE TRAditionally

annotation.surface: A dish that customarily comes with fish.
annotation.walkthrough: The plate and the fish make a meal, but the fish is the answer and a tiny aquarium one.
annotation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small, brightly coloured tropical fish.

entries.clue: Right structural unit housing books, computers, etc (11)

indicatorNotes.housing: to house something is to give it a roof, keep it inside, so ELEMENT holds NT and IT

blocks.note: an element is a component, a unit of a structure
NT = New Testament, a set of books
IT = information technology, computers and the like

annotation.surface: A proper building block that stores books and computers.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'etc' matters: IT covers computers and all their kin. 'Right' opens the clue as if it were a direction; it is the noun, a claim you are owed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a legal or moral right to receive something, such as holiday or benefits, is an entitlement.

entries.clue: Tabloid lying about New York prosecutor and Irish police officer (5)

indicatorNotes.about: turns RAG about, so it reads backwards

blocks.note: rag = a trashy newspaper; 'lying' is its reputation, not an instruction
DA = District Attorney, the US prosecutor

annotation.surface: A dishonest paper's story about a New York DA and an Irish officer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lying about' reads as 'telling lies about'; 'about' alone reverses the rag.
